notes.backticks-fewer: inside backticks a name goes in with one backslash fewer than in 6.46: the same words for the remote shell
notes.bang: a ! in a name: on the line TAB writes \\! where 6.46 wrote \\\! (the Enter tests check the word mssh gets); inside $( ) 6.46 gave the remote shell the name with a literal backslash (zz\!x) and 6.47 gives zz!x, the ! outside the quote ("\!"); inside backticks the words are the same at Enter (the harness's own reading of the line differs), with two backslashes fewer on the line
notes.dollar-home: inside backticks the \$ of \$HOME is read by them: 6.46 offered this machine's home names, which is what that shell expands there; 6.47 offers none (nothing wrong goes in)
notes.typed-backslashes: a backslash typed in a directory stays as typed on the line and in $( ); 6.46 wrote it again, one more (the same words for the remote shell)
notes.ticked-directory: inside backticks TAB goes on into a directory written for them (6.46 stopped before it)
notes.dd-tilde: a ~/ or ~name/ typed after an =, as dd's if= has it, stays as typed in a quoted command (6.46 wrote this machine's home there); whether the remote shell expands that ~ is its own: bash does, dash and zsh do not
notes.quoted-directory: a directory holding a $, or typed in a quote of the quoted command, goes on (6.46 offered nothing there)
notes.typed-backslashes-ticked: a backslash typed in a directory stays as typed inside backticks; 6.46 wrote one backslash fewer than typed (the same words for the remote shell)

unpinned.time: the remote words hold the time of the run
unpinned.bang: a name holding ! on the line: zsh's history expansion reads the words at Enter, which no harness here does; test_zsh_a_name_holding_an_exclamation_mark_in_a_double_quoted_command_reaches_the_remote_shell_as_named checks the words at Enter
unpinned.local-home: the remote words hold this machine's HOME, a directory of the run: a backtick reads the line in this shell (a \$HOME there is this machine's)
unpinned.unreadable: the harness reads no words from the line (a redirect or a parenthesis is left in it), which the test checks
unpinned.open-quote: a quote is left open in the line: the words the harness's sh makes of it differ from one image to the next
unpinned.sh-tilde: the words hold the harness's sh's reading of a ~+ (an sh that is bash expands it, dash does not)

omitted.q40b: mssh h " with TAB and nothing else: the harness reads no line from it (None, as in 6.46)

cases.typed: mssh h "echo hi | grep x zz
